Definition: properly, to be dense, i.e. tough or severe (in various applications)
BiblicalUsage: Hard is the word for a stiff neck and a heavy yoke: circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked; thy father made our yoke grievous, now therefore make the grievous service lighter. Elisha is told, thou hast asked a hard thing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hardness is the resistance of the heart to God, and the cure is the circumcision of the heart, not the lightening of the load. The yoke stays heavy until the neck is soft, and that is why the same word covers both.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
